products.name: CoCounsel (Casetext)
products.note: Legal research AI; litigation support; Westlaw integration; attorney work product risk

reading.body:
Thomson Reuters positions legal AI as a workflow accelerator for attorneys handling research, litigation, and drafting, with CoCounsel integrated into its Westlaw platform and a newly launched proprietary language model called Thomson announced in August 2026.

The company frames CoCounsel around what it calls "Fiduciary-Grade AI," a term meant to address the high stakes of legal work product. The product is moving toward agentic workflows capable of multi-step tasks, suggesting a shift from single-query assistance to autonomous handling of complex litigation sequences. A reported case study shows 100% increase in litigation capacity, though this reflects a single firm's claim rather than systematic measurement across the market.

Thomson Reuters' launch of its own language model in 2026 signals a move away from reliance on third-party foundation models for legal applications. This matters because legal work involves privileged information, and companies handling such data face pressure to internalize model training and inference. The data does not specify whether Thomson is used in CoCounsel, whether it runs on Thomson Reuters' own infrastructure, or how its compute requirements compare to the company's existing platform operations.

The data covers one tracked product and does not show Thomson Reuters' full portfolio of AI applications, revenue contribution, or total infrastructure footprint. It does not indicate whether CoCounsel's workflows run on Thomson Reuters' own data centers, cloud services, or both, leaving the relationship between this product and the company's underlying power and building constraints unclear.

profile_text.body:
Thomson Reuters is a publicly traded global content and technology company, listed on both Nasdaq and the TSX under the ticker TRI, and headquartered in Toronto. The company describes itself as delivering purpose-built technology that empowers professionals in the legal, tax, accounting, risk, fraud, and government sectors to make faster decisions and gain sharper insights. Its platform connects tools across tax, trade, legal, and risk through a suite it calls ONESOURCE+, which is positioned as an AI-powered connected approach for compliance and risk teams.

The company's primary AI product is CoCounsel, described on its site as professional-grade legal AI built on what Thomson Reuters calls Fiduciary-Grade AI principles, and grounded in content from Westlaw and Practical Law. CoCounsel is designed for legal research, drafting, and multi-step litigation workflows, and the site reports that a firm called Justly Prudent used CoCounsel and Westlaw AI to increase litigation capacity by 100%. Global law firm Greenberg Traurig, LLP is cited as having deployed the next generation of CoCounsel Legal as of August 26, 2026. Thomson Reuters also announced on August 24, 2026, the launch of Thomson, described as the company's first proprietary large language model developed in-house. Separately, the company offers AI-powered Harmonized System code classification tools for trade compliance under its ONESOURCE+ umbrella.

The held facts identify the company as a for-profit public company incorporated with the SEC under CIK 0001075124, with a founding date recorded as 2008. CoCounsel traces to the Casetext acquisition noted in the product registry, where it is catalogued under the Finance and Legal AI category with noted applications in legal research, litigation support, and Westlaw integration.
